item.title: The Everyday Miracles of Rinko Kawauchi
item.description: The photographer takes the smallest moments and finds in them a universe, passing her unwavering attention on to us.

item.title: Why an Influential Stylist Turned to AI
item.description: After retiring from a career in fashion, Simon Foxton was lured back into image-making by fresh faces. The only catch is, they don’t exist.

item.title: A Brazilian Photographer Seeks the Liberation of Desire
item.description: Fe Avila makes a world of raw, unmediated freedom where humans are stripped to their primal essence, unbound by hierarchy or control.

item.title: Takashi Homma on His Photobook Philosophy
item.description: Since the 1990s, Homma has chronicled the vagaries of fashion and youth culture, suburban life, and radioactive mushrooms, amassing more than sixty publications.

item.title: Dionne Lee Is Reinventing the Landscape Photograph
item.description: In "Dionne Lee: Currents," the photographer speaks about the interwoven histories of land, power, survival, and Black identity.

item.title: How Jo Ractliffe Became a Leading Photographer of Postapartheid South Africa
item.description: From her Cape Town studio, Jo Ractliffe reflects on photographing the aftermath of violence—the subject of her new exhibition “Out of Place.”

item.title: Inside a Minneapolis Newspaper’s Coverage of the ICE Raids
item.description: As ICE agents occupied the Twin Cities in January 2026, The Minnesota Star Tribune deployed local photographers to tell a national story.

item.title: The Emotional Saturation of William Eggleston’s “Last Dyes”
item.description: In the David Zwirner exhibition "The Last Dyes," the intensity of color in the photographer's dye-transfer prints is rarified and precise.

item.title: Jack Pierson Revisits His Miami Moment
item.description: For his exhibition "The Miami Years" at the Bass, Pierson returns to South Beach, presenting photographs, paintings, and '80s-era memories.

item.title: Takuma Nakahira’s Essential Writing on Photography
item.description: "At the Limits of the Gaze": A crucial figure in the “Provoke” era of Japanese photography, Nakahira also wrote essays brimming with urgency.

item.title: Lemaire’s Designers on the Narrative Power of Clothes
item.description: The Paris-based fashion duo talks about what inspires them, from August Sander to scooter riders in Hanoi.

item.title: The World According to Guido Guidi
item.description: The Italian photographer and Renaissance man channels his training as an architect, painter, and draughtsman into quiet studies of European towns and landscapes.

item.title: Hashem Shakeri’s Portrait of a Climate Hotspot in Iran
item.description: From Aperture’s “The End of Nature?” issue: A photographer chronicles the art of everyday survival in the drylands of Balochistan.

item.title: The Remains of a Handmade Utopia
item.description: In the wooded enclaves of Northern California, Michael Schmelling documents what’s left of the 1960s back-to-the-land movement.

item.title: Announcing the 2026 Aperture Portfolio Prize Shortlist
item.description: Here are the shortlisted artists for the 2026 Aperture Portfolio Prize, which aims to spotlight new talent in contemporary photography.
